rationales: Karl Lohmann was not awarded the Nobel Prize in 1940.
Karl Lohmann was not awarded the Nobel Prize in 1941.
The 1958 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to other scientists, not Karl Lohmann.
Karl Lohmann was not awarded the Nobel Prize in 1986.
Ground tissue is primarily composed of parenchyma cells.
Vessel elements are water-conducting xylem cells, not ground tissue cells.
Tracheids are water-conducting xylem cells, not ground tissue cells.
Sieve tubes are sugar-conducting phloem cells, not ground tissue cells.
Fungal cell walls are generally not made of cellulose.
Chitin is the main structural material in fungal cell walls.
Lignin is found mainly in the walls of woody plants.
Peptidoglycan is characteristic of bacterial cell walls.
A family is a group of related genera.
A genus contains related species, not related genera.
A class contains related orders, not genera directly.
A phylum contains related classes, not genera directly.
Deductions are conclusions drawn from observations or premises, not tested hypotheses.
Hypotheses supported repeatedly by evidence may develop into theories.
Observations are recorded findings, not hypotheses that have stood the test of time.
Laws describe consistent patterns but are not simply hypotheses that have stood the test of time.
Anatomy studies the internal structure of organisms.
Morphology studies the form and structure of organisms.
Histology studies the microscopic structure of tissues.
Physiology studies how organisms and their parts function.
A blood pH of 4.7 is far too acidic for normal blood.
A blood pH of 6.7 is below the normal range.
Normal blood pH is about 7.4.
A blood pH of 5.4 is far too acidic for normal blood.
The pericycle is a narrow layer of cells just outside the conducting tissues in a root.
The endodermis lies outside the pericycle and forms the inner boundary of the cortex.
Xylem is a conducting tissue, not the layer outside the conducting tissues.
Phloem is a conducting tissue, not the layer outside the conducting tissues.
Nitrogen is a macronutrient required in relatively large amounts.
Zinc is a micronutrient required in small amounts.
Magnesium is a macronutrient required in relatively large amounts.
Potassium is a macronutrient required in relatively large amounts.
The stroma is the fluid-filled region of the chloroplast, not where chlorophyll is located.
Chlorophyll is embedded in the thylakoid membranes.
The plasma membrane is not the site of chlorophyll in leaf cells.
The cytoplasm is not where chlorophyll is located.
Substrates are the molecules on which enzymes act.
Biocatalysts are enzymes themselves, not the molecules they act upon.
Products are formed by enzyme-catalyzed reactions.
Catalysts speed reactions and are not the specific molecules acted upon by enzymes.
Meiosis is a reduction division used in sexual reproduction, not the usual division of prokaryotes.
Multiple fission is not the typical prokaryotic cell division process.
Prokaryotic cells typically divide by binary fission.
Budding is not the typical division process of prokaryotic cells.
Fibrinogen is mainly involved in blood clotting.
Albumin helps maintain the osmotic balance of blood.
Haemoglobin transports oxygen in red blood cells.
Globulins have various roles, including transport and immune defense, but albumin chiefly maintains blood water balance.
The cortex is a broader region outside the endodermis, not a single layer surrounding the pericycle.
The endodermis is the single cell layer surrounding the pericycle and vascular cylinder.
Xylem is a conducting tissue within the vascular cylinder.
Phloem is a conducting tissue within the vascular cylinder.
Iron is a micronutrient required in small amounts.
Boron is a micronutrient required in small amounts.
Chlorine is a micronutrient required in small amounts.
Oxygen is a macronutrient required in large amounts by plants.
